title: National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2027
official_title: Making appropriations for national security, Department of State, and related programs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: The sponsor is a Republican in the Republican-majority House and the bill passed the House with no cosponsors, as is typical for an appropriations measure. Standalone appropriations bills are generally reconciled with a Senate version or folded into a broader package before enactment, and Senate passage would require 60 votes.
summary: This bill provides fiscal year 2027 funding for the Department of State, foreign assistance, and related international programs. It sets specific amounts for diplomacy, global health, humanitarian aid, and security assistance, and attaches policy conditions to many of those funds.
brief: Funds the Department of State and U.S. foreign operations for fiscal year 2027.

top_lines.headline: Diplomacy and State Operations
subs: Funds embassy operations, worldwide security, and consular activities

top_lines.headline: Global Health and Humanitarian Aid
subs: $3.35B for global health and $5.53B for HIV/AIDS programs
$1.25B contribution to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria
$5B for international humanitarian and refugee assistance

top_lines.headline: Security and Economic Assistance
subs: $1.66B for international narcotics control and law enforcement

sections.label: Title I - Department of State Operations

items.main: Provides $9.76B for Diplomatic Programs, the Department of State's main operating account.
items.detail: Of that amount, up to $4.16B remains available until expended for overseas operations and $738.6M is for Worldwide Security Protection. The title also funds embassy security and construction, the Harry S Truman Building, and educational and cultural exchange programs.

items.main: Provides $3.35B for global health programs and an additional $5.53B for HIV/AIDS, including a $1.25B U.S. contribution to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria.
items.detail: The global health funds carry conditions barring money to organizations that support coercive abortion or involuntary sterilization and restricting family-planning assistance. The title also provides $5B for international humanitarian assistance, of which not less than $2.75B is for disaster relief.

items.main: Provides $6.89B for National Security Investment Programs and funds several development agencies.
items.detail: At least 15 percent of the National Security Investment Programs funds must go to programs in Africa. The title also provides $830M for the Millennium Challenge Corporation, $410.5M for the Peace Corps, and $205.2M for the Democracy Fund.

items.main: Provides $6.75B for the Foreign Military Financing program of nonrepayable grants for defense articles and services.
items.detail: NATO members and major non-NATO allies may use the funds for procurement not sold through the U.S. government. The title also provides $1.66B for international narcotics control and law enforcement, $870M for nonproliferation, anti-terrorism, and demining, and $119.2M for international military education and training.

sections.label: Titles V-VII - Multilateral Assistance and General Provisions

items.main: Funds multilateral assistance and export programs and sets government-wide policy conditions and rescissions.
items.detail: Title V funds international financial institutions and Title VI funds export and investment assistance. Title VII carries the bill's general provisions, including reporting and notification requirements, policy restrictions, and rescissions of portions of prior-year unobligated balances.

underreported.section: Title III - Global Health Programs (family-planning provisos)
underreported.summary: Bars global health funds to any organization the President determines supports or manages coercive abortion or involuntary sterilization, and sets detailed conditions on voluntary family-planning projects.
underreported.why_unreported: These are substantive abortion-related policy conditions attached to a health appropriations line, beyond the funding amounts themselves.

underreported.section: Title III - International Humanitarian Assistance (Israel earmark)
underreported.summary: Earmarks not less than $6.5M of the $5B humanitarian account for refugees resettling in Israel.
underreported.why_unreported: A specific country earmark sits within a general humanitarian and refugee account.

underreported.summary: Rescinds portions of prior-year unobligated balances alongside the new appropriations.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill claws back previously appropriated funds in addition to setting fiscal year 2027 amounts, offsetting part of the new spending.

gaps: The bill provides $6.75B in Foreign Military Financing grants but does not set country allocations in the text, leaving them to notification procedures.
The bill provides $5B for international humanitarian assistance but earmarks only disaster relief and Israel refugees, leaving allocation of the balance unspecified in the text.
The bill funds a National Security Investment Programs account but does not define that program beyond the Foreign Assistance Act authorities it cites.
The bill rescinds portions of prior-year balances but does not identify in the summary which programs those balances were originally appropriated for.

removed: Rescinds portions of prior-year unobligated balances (Title VII)
